name: MINOS
description: We present MINOS, a simulator designed to support the development of multisensory models for goal-directed navigation in complex indoor environments. The simulator leverages large datasets of complex 3D environments and supports flexible configuration of multimodal sensor suites. We use MINOS to benchmark deep-learning-based navigation methods, to analyze the influence of environmental complexity on navigation performance, and to carry out a controlled study of multimodality in sensorimotor learning. The experiments show that current deep reinforcement learning approaches fail in large realistic environments. The experiments also indicate that multimodality is beneficial in learning to navigate cluttered scenes. MINOS is released open-source to the research community at http://minosworld.org . A video that shows MINOS can be found at https://youtu.be/c0mL9K64q84
typical_sota_score: often <50% task success rate in large realistic environments (varies widely with task and sensors)
reputation: MINOS is a well-known early embodied navigation simulator used in research on multimodal and goal-directed navigation.
notes: Non-LLM robotics/simulation benchmark; results are environment- and setup-dependent, and the original paper emphasizes that many deep RL methods struggle in realistic large-scale indoor scenes.
